facts.label: Passivo presente
facts.sub: Use is/are + particípio para nome, material e uso: It is called the Capitol. It is made of stone. Tacos are sold here.

facts.label: Nome
facts.sub: Para dar o nome de algo, use is/are called: It is called the Capitol. Para perguntar, diga What is it called? Em PT é “como se chama”.

facts.label: Material
facts.sub: Para falar do material, use is/are made of: It is made of stone. Se o material muda, use made from. Para ingredientes, use made with: They are made with corn.

compare.ask: It is called the Capitol. It is made of stone.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “chama-se” e “é feito de” para falar de coisas.
compare.tip: Diga: “It is called the Capitol. It is made of stone.”
compare.us: Em inglês: It is called… It is made of… It is used for… Use is/are + particípio, sem falar de quem faz.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: It is called the Capitol. It is made of stone.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: The passive uses is/are + past participle.
We say “It is make of stone”.
items.why: We say It is made of stone.

items.s: Tacos are sold here is passive.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: The passive uses is/are + past participle. → Verdadeiro (Yes: is made, is called.)
We say “It is make of stone”. → Falso (We say It is made of stone.)
Tacos are sold here is passive. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: Downtown Austin · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a sunny afternoon in downtown Austin. People walk under tall trees. Paulo holds a paper map. A police officer, Grace, smiles at him. She knows the city well. She offers to help.
“Hi, Paulo! Welcome to Austin. Can I help you?” says Grace. “Yes, please. What is this big building called?” says Paulo. “It is called the Capitol. It is made of pink stone.” says Grace.
